messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 - GPU pool exhaustion reported for us-west-1. Queue growth detected. Auto-escalating to on-call.

Eve_Oncall: seeing massive queue build in us-west-gpu-pool. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/GPUPool us-west queue len ~120 -> 5min avg 85. Throttle% ~96%. Anyone touching continuous batching or prefix cache in last hour?

Sam_Infra: I rolled out a config change to continuous-batching yesterday to reduce latency — changed `batch_max_delay_ms` from `200` -> `10` for a subset of models (canary). Noted increased requests but didn't expect queue spike. Rolling that back now.

Maria_SRE: coming in. Adding pager and handoff. @Eve_Oncall please hand to me once you confirm rollback status. Customer-ops, can you confirm any customer-facing errors?

Customer-Ops: several customers reported 503s and rate limits. CID: acme-inc reported failures in /v1/generate around 21:12 UTC, error rate ~27% for them. Support ticket #12456 opened.

Zach_Runtime: logs show a flood of small batches and KV cache misses. Prefix cache miss rate spiked from 2% -> 78% at 21:08. Prefetch TTL for `prefix-cache` was set to `0s` in the same canary applied by infra. That would explain cache coldness.

Eve_Oncall: I started rollback of the canary to previous continuous-batching config at 21:15. Command: `kubectl -n runtime set configmap batching-config --from-file=batching.yaml=./bak/batching-2026-03-14.yaml` — deploy-bot triggered redeploy.

Deploy-Bot: Redeploy triggered for runtime/batching-config canary -> stable. Rollout status: 4/4 pods updated, 0/4 not ready. (21:18)

Sam_Infra: I also noticed autoscaler reached `scale_cap` for the GPU pool (configured cap 64). At peak we had 64 nodes allocated and queue kept growing. Autoscaler didn't add more due to cap. Requesting temporary increase to 96.

Maria_SRE: Approved. Sam, submit quota bump in infra-prod for us-west GPU pool to 96 and patch autoscaler. Meanwhile, manual spin-up of 10 reserve GPUs to alleviate pressure.

Sam_Infra: Manual scale up command executed: `infractl gpu reserve --region us-west --count 10 --label temp-relief` (21:21). New pool size 74/96. Monitoring.

Eve_Oncall: After rollback and reserve nodes, queue decreased from 120 -> 34 in 12 minutes. Throttle% down to 22%, error rate for CID acme-inc down to 3%. Good sign. Continuing to monitor for prefix cache warmup.

Zach_Runtime: Warming prefix cache by replaying recent prefixes from hot-requests: `python tools/warm_prefix_cache.py --lookback 30m --concurrency 8` — running now. Expect hit-rate to recover in ~10-15m.

Customer-Ops: Notifying affected customers: acme-inc and beta-saas notified via status page and direct outreach. ETA for full recovery: 30-45 min.

Maria_SRE: Incident timeline so far logged. Root causes likely (1) canary change to `batch_max_delay_ms` producing smaller batches and higher per-token overhead, (2) inadvertent `prefix-cache` TTL set to 0 causing miss storm, (3) autoscaler cap set too low for increased request fanout.

Eve_Oncall: Next actions: (A) keep autoscaler cap at 96 for 2 hours, (B) revert continuous batching canary permanently until we instrument request distribution, (C) set `prefix-cache.ttl` back to `10m`, (D) add guard in deploy pipeline to prevent TTL=0 for prefix cache, (E) customer follow-ups.

Maria_SRE: On-call handoff inbound: I'm taking this for night shift. @Eve_Oncall I have notes and the rollback steps confirmed. If queue rises >50 again or throttle% >40, page me directly.

Eve_Oncall: handing off +1. Incident severity remains SEV2 until full recovery and postmortem scheduled. :white_check_mark:

Maria_SRE: Created incident doc: https://wiki.redwood.internal/incidents/3445007777-gpu-drought-prefixttl. Postmortem assigned to @Sam_Infra and @Zach_Runtime. Closing pager but monitoring for 2 hours.

Incidents-Bot: Incident annotated: mitigated at 21:34 UTC. Summary: rollback batching canary, prefix-cache TTL revert, manual scale-up. Follow-up: postmortem due in 48h.
